guard: an isolated worker can die without taking the custodial child PID with it, a successor can adopt the surviving seat, a childless custodian exits on its own, and reap never treats record identities as proof of process-tree disappearance
why: The reap cells cover a live custodied seat, mismatched identities, a forged same-uid process-group leader and a setsid escapee whose custodian has exited.
The lifecycle boot cells rewrite a live seat's record to name a foreign boot and to omit its boot id; both outcomes are retained, never thrown.

mutations.name: M1 suppress worker-death survival
mutations.expectRed: worker death leaves the custodial child PID running
mutations.cell: worker death leaves the custodial child PID running
mutations.note: The mutation is only the final child-live predicate after the worker is proven dead.

mutations.name: M2 re-apply hello geometry on every later
mutations.expectRed: resize: geometry survives the hello apply
mutations.cell: resize: geometry survives the hello apply
mutations.note: Unconditional hello apply is the clobber that made mesh-attach-plane miss a 90x25 resize.

mutations.name: M3 notify exit only to output subscribers
mutations.find: for (const sock of controllers) send(sock, { event: "exit", exit });
mutations.expectRed: onExit fires without an output subscription
mutations.cell: onExit fires without an output subscription
mutations.note: Manager readiness onExit does not subscribe to output. Output-only notify is the CI M3 process-exit miss.

mutations.name: M4 skip already-dead onExit
mutations.expectRed: onExit fires for a child that exits before hello
mutations.cell: onExit fires for a child that exits before hello
mutations.note: A child that exits before attach must still fire onExit. Manager readiness uses that path without an output subscription.

mutations.name: M5 skip subscribe output replay
mutations.find: if (early) send(sock, { event: "output", sub, data: Buffer.from(early, "utf8").toString("base64") });
mutations.expectRed: fast-exit print reaches onData before onExit
mutations.cell: fast-exit print reaches onData before onExit
mutations.note: launchSeat returns after the child pid exists, so dump-then-exit bytes are already written. Live subscribe without replay is the env-isolate empty capture.

mutations.name: M6 leave the controller socket open after waitForExit
mutations.expectRed: waitForExit drops the controller socket so the worker can exit
mutations.cell: waitForExit drops the controller socket so the worker can exit
mutations.note: A live Unix socket after waitForExit keeps the manager event loop alive through spawn-detach teardown.

mutations.name: M7 skip terminal custodian cleanup after child exit
mutations.find:
const settleTerminal = (): void => {
    if (alive || settling || !ready) return;
mutations.expectRed: natural exit: custodian process and socket converge and the record is retained without fixture kill
mutations.cell: natural exit: custodian process and socket converge and the record is retained without fixture kill
mutations.note: Deleting the owned terminal-settle transition leaves the Unix server, socket, and custodian process alive after waitForExit. The named cell must fail without fixture SIGKILL.

mutations.name: restoring a record-named kill violates forged record protection
mutations.find: const { stop, error } = await requestStop(root, id, rec, opts.graceMs ?? 10_000);
mutations.expectRed: a forged same-uid record is retained and its process-group leader is never signalled
mutations.cell: a forged same-uid record is retained and its process-group leader is never signalled
mutations.note: A same-uid record can forge a live pid and matching start token; reap must never signal it. The replace signals only through a pidfd checked against the record's start token, never a numeric pid or group.

mutations.name: an empty session census returns reaped for a setsid escapee
mutations.expectRed: a setsid escapee keeps the reap retained and is never signalled
mutations.cell: a setsid escapee keeps the reap retained and is never signalled
mutations.note: An empty process-group census cannot establish that a detached descendant is gone.

mutations.name: a foreign-boot record cannot throw
mutations.find: const { stop, error } = await requestStop(root, id, rec, opts.graceMs ?? 10_000);
mutations.replace:
if (rec.bootId !== undefined && rec.bootId !== readFileSync("/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id", "utf8").trim()) throw new Error("foreign boot");
  const { stop, error } = await requestStop(root, id, rec, opts.graceMs ?? 10_000);
mutations.expectRed: a foreign boot record is retained instead of throwing
mutations.cell: a foreign boot record is retained instead of throwing
mutations.note: Throwing only on the foreign-boot path must redden the retained-outcome cell.

mutations.name: joining an unchecked custody id escapes the root
mutations.expectRed: a forged custody id that walks out of the root is refused, not resolved
mutations.cell: a forged custody id that walks out of the root is refused, not resolved

mutations.name: T1 settle unlinks the custody record (natural exit)
mutations.expectRed: natural exit: custodian process and socket converge and the record is retained without fixture kill
mutations.cell: natural exit: custodian process and socket converge and the record is retained without fixture kill
mutations.note: Restoring the pre-T1 unlink forgets custody of a seat whose processes nothing has proved gone.

mutations.name: T1 settle unlinks the custody record (unadopted)
mutations.expectRed: its socket is gone with it and its record is retained
mutations.cell: its socket is gone with it and its record is retained
mutations.note: The same unlink on the unobserved-handoff settle path.

mutations.name: T1 drop the graceful SIGKILL escalation
mutations.expectRed: graceful stop escalates: a child ignoring SIGTERM is gone after waitForExit
mutations.cell: graceful stop escalates: a child ignoring SIGTERM is gone after waitForExit
mutations.note: Without the timer a SIGTERM-ignoring child outlives a graceful stop.

mutations.name: T1 kill an unpinned child by bare pid
mutations.replace:
const pidfd = dropPidfd ? undefined : term._pidfd;
  if (typeof pidfd !== "number") process.kill(term.pid, "SIGKILL");
mutations.expectRed: an unpinned child is never signalled: launch fails, no socket or record, the child lives unmarked
mutations.cell: an unpinned child is never signalled: launch fails, no socket or record, the child lives unmarked
mutations.note: The proc.kill fallback: a send by pid to a child this process cannot name.

mutations.name: T1 a listen error escapes the startup SIGKILL
mutations.expectRed: startup failure (listen-error) after pinning stops the child
mutations.cell: startup failure (listen-error) after pinning stops the child
mutations.note: An unhandled listen error kills the custodian without a send; the child ignores the hangup and survives.

mutations.name: T1 drop the startup-failure SIGKILL
mutations.expectRed: startup failure (after-bind) after pinning stops the child
mutations.cell: startup failure (after-bind) after pinning stops the child
mutations.note: A failure after bind exits the custodian with the child still under it.

mutations.name: T1 the custodian recreates its seat directory
mutations.replace:
await holdAt("before-fs");
  (await import("node:fs")).mkdirSync((await import("node:path")).dirname(launch.socket), { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
mutations.expectRed: a removed seat directory stops a late custodian: no record, no directory, the child is gone
mutations.cell: a removed seat directory stops a late custodian: no record, no directory, the child is gone
mutations.note: Restoring runCustodian's mkdirSync lets a late custodian resurrect a seat its manager already removed.

mutations.name: T1 the custodian ignores a sealed fence
mutations.expectRed: a sealed fence refuses the launch: no child, no socket, no record
mutations.cell: a sealed fence refuses the launch: no child, no socket, no record
mutations.note: A seal written after the launcher's check must still stop the spawn.

mutations.name: T1 open the startup-failure handle by pid after the hold
mutations.replace:
const st = readFileSync(`/proc/${proc.pid}/stat`, "utf8").slice(readFileSync(`/proc/${proc.pid}/stat`, "utf8").lastIndexOf(") ") + 2).split(" ");
      if (st[0] !== "Z" && Number(st[1]) === process.pid) process.kill(proc.pid, "SIGKILL");
mutations.expectRed: a reused pid is never signalled: the process that retook the child's pid outlives the startup failure
mutations.cell: a reused pid is never signalled: the process that retook the child's pid outlives the startup failure
mutations.note: A pid-addressed send guarded by parent and liveness checks: a CLONE_PARENT process at the reused pid passes both.

mutations.name: write the custody record without the boot it belongs to
mutations.expectRed: the custodian stamps the boot its pids belong to
mutations.cell: the custodian stamps the boot its pids belong to
mutations.note: An unstamped record is refused by reapSeat, so every seat this custodian launches becomes unreapable rather than misreaped.

mutations.name: an unanswered stop request never times out
mutations.expectRed: a custodian socket that never answers times out the stop within graceMs, still retained
mutations.cell: a custodian socket that never answers times out the stop within graceMs, still retained
mutations.note: Without the bound a silent socket would hang the reap, and with it a manager terminal.

mutations.name: the seat preference write is skipped
mutations.expectRed: oom: the custodial child carries the seat preference
mutations.cell: oom: the custodial child carries the seat preference
mutations.note: Skipping the write leaves the child at the 600 the launcher raised itself to before the launch, so the read-back mismatches the target, the helper reports applied:false and the child cell reddens on every host, including a runner whose processes start at 500.

mutations.name: the preference is written to the custodian instead of the child
mutations.expectRed: oom: the custodian keeps the launcher's inherited oom_score_adj
mutations.cell: oom: the custodian keeps the launcher's inherited oom_score_adj
mutations.note: The write lands on the custodian's own pid instead of the child's; the child then also reads 0, but the custodian cell is the one that distinguishes the wrong target from a skipped write. The launcher sits at 600 before the launch, so a custodian that receives the write reads 500 against the launcher's 600 and the custodian cell reddens on every host.
